officialRevision: Cloud Firestore Security Rules limits (Usage and limits); Manage and deploy Firebase Security Rules; Security Rules behavior (Cloud Storage)

limits.officialText: Maximum number of exists(), get(), and getAfter() calls per request: 10 for single-document requests and query requests
limits.notes: Cached calls do not count; the cache scope is fixed by conformance.

limits.officialText: Maximum number of exists(), get(), and getAfter() calls per request: 20 for multi-document reads, transactions, and batched writes
The additional limit of 10 applies to each operation in a multi-document request
Maximum number of nested match statement levels: 10
Maximum path length, in path segments, allowed within a set of nested match statements: 100
limits.notes: Recursive wildcard segment counting is fixed by boundary fixtures.

limits.officialText: Maximum number of path capture variables allowed within a set of nested match statements: 20

limits.notes: Checked statically on the call graph and at runtime.

limits.officialText: Maximum number of let variable bindings per function: 10
Maximum number of recursive or cyclical function calls: 0 (not permitted)
limits.notes: Strongly connected component check on the call graph.

limits.officialText: Maximum number of expressions evaluated per request: 1,000
limits.notes: Runtime budget, not AST node count.

limits.officialText: Rulesets must be smaller than 256 KiB of text when serialized (Manage and deploy Firebase Security Rules)
limits.notes: Serialized UTF-8 size of the Source; multi-file framing overhead fixed by projects.test conformance.

limits.officialText: Maximum size of a ruleset: 250 KB (compiled)
limits.notes: Backend representation is not public; local values are estimates with lower/point/upper bounds.

limits.officialText: Maximum number of deployed rulesets per project: 2,500
limits.notes: Exact counter when managed locally; remote projects via oracle ledger.

limits.officialText: Cloud Storage Security Rules may call firestore.exists() and firestore.get() at most 2 times per request
limits.notes: Separate catalog entry; never merged with the Firestore Rules document access budget.
